newsitem.title: UK: Jardine Matheson says business in line.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Matheson says business in line.

text.p: International trading group Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd said on Thursday that most of its businesses had performed in line with expectations in the year to date.

"Trading results will, however, be affected by a reduced contribution from Jardine Fleming, which continues to perform at the lower level seen in the second half of 1996," chairman Henry Keswick said in a statement.
Keswick said the overall group result would be enhanced by an exceptional profit from the sale of Jardine Pacific's life insurance business.
Last August Jardine Fleming, which is jointly held by Jardine Matheson and British investment bank Robert Fleming, was involved in a scandal involving its fund management business in Hong Kong.

The joint venture lost key clients as a result of the affair, which led to heavy regulatory penalties and a rash of resignations. Fund industry sources said it could take some time for Jardine Fleming to recover.
In March, Jardine Matheson said its 1996 net profits fell to $300.2 million compared with $420 million the previous year.

At the time of the results, Keswick said actions taken to refine and strengthen its business, should enable the company to maintain a steady trading result in 1997 and he looked forward to improved earnings growth in subsequent years.
